subject: koala
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: koala gripping a eucalyptus branch stand.
Style: pixel art.
reasoning:
Looking at the renders, I notice the koala isn't gripping the branch properly—it appears to float above the trunk fork rather than hugging it, with the body positioned too high relative to the trunk.

The arm shapes are rendering as odd broken wedges rather than natural limbs, since the shoulder-to-elbow and elbow-to-wrist segments angle awkwardly in different directions. I should simplify these into straighter rods that reach cleanly from shoulder to the branch, and pull the koala's body back so it sits flush against the fork instead of perched on top.

I'm checking the collision between the body depth and the fork limbs' position at the crotch height - the body is clipping into the limbs, so I need to either shift the fork further back (around z=-0.2 to -0.24) or pull the body back so the surfaces touch without overlapping. The arms will then need to wrap outward and forward from the shoulder to meet the branch's actual x-position.

Working out finger positions wrapping around the limb...

Also reconsidering the arm geometry since slanted box frustums create ugly shards at the joint ends—thinking about swapping to rod sections with a square ngon profile to keep the blocky pixel style without the artifacts.

Simpler plan: a helper that builds a box oriented from one joint to another by direction and length, overlapping cubes at the joints to hide seams. I'll apply this same approach to the legs, positioning hips, knees, and ankles so the feet land correctly on the branch now that it's shifted behind the koala.

I'm checking the coordinates carefully to make sure the feet, hip box, and crotch box don't clip through each other or through the limb geometry as everything gets repositioned.

Since all the trunk and root pieces are keyed to a shared FORK_Z constant, I just need to update that one value and verify the plinth, trunk, and surrounding rocks/nuts still sit at reasonable depths relative to it.

The branch V might be too wide and tall for the koala, so I'm considering shrinking FORK_H and FORK_X slightly while keeping it believable. For the face, the eyes and nose need resizing — the nose box looks oversized and square rather than rounded, so I should scale it down and reposition it for a more natural koala muzzle.

I'm rethinking the shoulder shards (frustum box arms) and the elbow/knee fluff boxes, which need repositioning or replacing to match new joint points, along with redesigning the claw grips so they don't point awkwardly backward. I also need to double-check the arm joint chain — three points for two spans seems off and needs a consistent wrist tip placement.

Confirming the joint naming is correct (shoulder, elbow, wrist as tip) and that parts bind properly to the wrist joint. Now I'm writing a helper function `limbBox` that builds a box geometry between two points, computing its length and direction so I can replace the repetitive arm/leg chain code with a cleaner reusable approach, then inserting it near the existing box helper definition.

Working out the actual arm joint coordinates — placing the shoulder, elbow, and wrist positions so the forearm bends naturally inward and downward toward the paw, checking that the wrist's z-depth lines up with the front face of the paw box so they overlap slightly rather than floating apart.

Now I'm building the hand geometry itself: a palm box attached at the wrist, with individual finger boxes spaced along the arm's width, each capped with a small claw segment, plus a thumb positioned on the inner side mirroring the outer fingers.

Moving to the legs, I'm defining hip, knee, and ankle joint positions along the branch centerline formula, then placing a foot box at the ankle to complete the limb structure.

I need to update the legs polyline to parent at the hips, then bump the eye size from 0.044 to 0.056 at y 0.868, and nudge the brow tick's y position from 0.892 to 0.9.

For the arms and legs section, I'll need to replace the whole block carefully since it must match exactly from the comment through the return statement -- copying it in full rather than trying to patch pieces, while keeping the armX reference intact.
